title: Porting the DID filter engine to JSON metadata added an Oracle branch that str.format()s user filter keys and values into a json_exists() expression wrapped in sqlalchemy text().

findings.explanation: Line 545 builds a SQLAlchemy text() query where user-supplied filter metadata is interpolated via .format(). The value is safely bound via .bindparams(val=...) and the $val placeholder, but the filter key (and json_column.key) is still interpolated directly into the SQL string. The key originates from user-provided filter dictionaries (_translate_filters, lines 243-261), i.e. user-controlled input can reach the query. The PR mitigates this by adding a strict whitelist regex at line 538 (re.match(r'^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$', key)) that raises DIDFilterSyntaxError for any non-alphanumeric/underscore key, so only whitelisted characters can be interpolated, and json_column.key is a server-defined model column name. Therefore the key is strictly validated against a whitelist and the value is bound, so this is very likely a false positive rather than an exploitable SQL injection.

The actual user-controlled value is passed only as a bound parameter (`:val AS "val"`), which is the safe path the rule itself recommends. Since the only user-controlled input to the query is bound via bindparams and every interpolated token is either internally generated or whitelist-validated, the finding is a false positive.
